subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted `/exec` session defaults be allowed to outlive and override later operator changes to `tools.exec`, or should operator security config invalidate or dominate those stored session fields?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally preserve `/exec` as per-session state, but the report shows that contract can shadow later stricter exec policy; automation cannot choose that security boundary safely.

options.title: Invalidate session exec defaults on policy changes
options.body: Track or detect exec-policy changes and clear or ignore persisted exec session fields with migration/reset coverage so operator hardening takes effect.

options.title: Keep documented session override semantics
options.body: Leave `/exec` persistence intact and document/tool the supported hard-disable path, accepting that `tools.exec` changes alone do not reset sessions.

options.title: Make global exec policy always win
options.body: Change resolver precedence so global/agent exec config overrides stored session fields, trading stronger enforcement for a broader breaking behavior change.

recommendation.title: Invalidate session exec defaults on policy changes
recommendation.body: Track or detect exec-policy changes and clear or ignore persisted exec session fields with migration/reset coverage so operator hardening takes effect.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant history ties the original `/exec` session override contract and resolver coverage to this owner.
